title: five-commands-the-map-cannot-render
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; each named charter's own owner gates its charter, and cairnmap owns the completeness rule being satisfied
intention: Five executables in bin/cmd — groundloop, mailcheck, operator, review, ruled — are commands no charter names, so the map cannot render them and the derivation gate reds. Each is named by the top-level `invoke` of the charter of the component its dispatcher actually execs, and /ruled is installed so the gate's sixth red clears too. No new charter is written: a thin dispatcher is not a component.
why: cairn/tools/cairnmap/cairnmap.py:336-351 walks bin/cmd and asks of each executable whether some charter's `invoke` names `cairn <name>`. The unnamed ones red with 'an undocumented command is impossible, by design' — the rule is that a command a reader cannot be briefed on does not exist for that reader, which is Law 5 at the command surface. Today five of 25 commands fail it, and the failure is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py carries a tooth (test_the_skill_class_derivation_gate_is_green) that reads the whole gate, so /intent's own proof has been standing at 8/9 for as long as these five have been unnamed. A skill whose proof cannot go green is a skill whose seal is a hypothesis.
how: Five one-field edits and one symlink; nothing new is created. (1) cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/intention+why.json — its `invoke` describes constructing GroundLoopDevice and names no command; append the operator face, `cairn groundloop status|start|stop|restart`, which bin/cmd/groundloop passes through verbatim to cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.cli. (2) cairn/devices/cc/intention+why.json — carries NO `invoke` key at all; add one naming `cairn mailcheck`, because every byte that command reads is ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail/, cc's own instance-space, and cc is therefore its owner even though the code sits in bin/cmd. (3) cairn/tools/operator_inbox/intention+why.json — `invoke` is the bare string 'cairn operator_inbox'; extend it to name `cairn operator` as well, the alias the whole corpus actually calls. (4) cairn/machines/skill_block/intention+why.json — its `invoke` already names `cairn skilldial`; add `cairn review` beside it, with its two forms (bare lists artifacts awaiting review; `cairn review <id> "words"` marks one reviewed). (5) skills/ruled/intention+why.json — `invoke` is '/ruled [<id>]', the slash face only; add the CLI face `cairn ruled [<id>]`, which execs skills.ruled.door. (6) Install /ruled: `ln -s ~/dev/src/cairn/skills/ruled ~/.claude/skills/ruled` — a symlink, matching all 14 standing entries; a copy would drift silently. (7) Poke cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh once, after the charter edits, before the crossing.
falsifier: DONE when (1) `./bin/cairn cairnmap --gate` exits 0 with zero findings across all seven checks; (2) each of the five commands is named by the top-level `invoke` of the charter of the component its dispatcher execs, and each such invoke carries the command's REAL usage — a checkable shape within 80 characters of the named command: a `<placeholder>`, a `sub|command` alternation, or the explicit words "no arguments" — so the gate's mention-check cannot be satisfied by a bare word. (REFINED DURING THE BUILD, 2026-09-11, and named here because the cast bar was unsatisfiable: the clause first read "at minimum one subcommand or argument the dispatcher actually accepts", and `bin/cmd/mailcheck` accepts NONE — it is a self-contained reader that takes no arguments. A bar no honest charter for mailcheck could clear would have forced either a false invoke or an exemption; the third shape admits the true answer instead, and still refuses a bare word.); (3) `python3 skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py` prints 13/13 teeth green (9 standing teeth plus the four this ticket declares), which requires /ruled installed as well as named; and (4) no new intention+why.json exists anywhere under bin/cmd/. WRONG INTENT if five charters appear under bin/cmd/ — a thin dispatcher is not a component, five new charters inflate the census by five with nothing behind them, and the design of `cairn groundloop` would then live somewhere other than where a mind stands to be briefed on the ground loop (Law 5). WRONG INTENT if /ruled is installed by copying rather than symlinking.

measured_at_cast: 2026-09-11, the full command-ownership census over the live corpus: 25 executables in bin/cmd, 75 charters, 79 invocable units (a unit is a charter plus any top-level facility block carrying its own `what`+`invoke`). 20 commands are owned, 5 are not. Of the 22 ownership SITES, 17 are the owning component's own top-level `invoke` naming the command (cairnmap, compile, determinism, edges, feedbackmap, install, operator_inbox, probescan, recordverdict, ruling, skilldial, sudorelay, test, tickets, whatsnext) and 5 are facility blocks on bin's charter (slate via session_open_program, turnscan via turn_shape_scan, askscan via prebuild_feedback_scan, deletegate and trash both via unrecoverable_delete_gate). ZERO commands are owned by a charter under bin/cmd/. Separately: `./bin/cairn cairnmap --gate` reports RED — 6 finding(s) (7 checks proved · 75 charters); the sixth is 'skill not installed: /ruled'. skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py prints 8/9, the one red being test_the_skill_class_derivation_gate_is_green. ~/.claude/skills holds 14 entries, every one a symlink into ~/dev/src/cairn/skills.
traces_to: Law 5 (intent, state and proofs share an address, and the address carries what a mind needs NOW — a command whose design is written nowhere near it cannot brief the mind standing there, which is what 'an undocumented command is impossible, by design' means); Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build could not pass — /intent's proof has stood at 8/9, so its green was never fully earned); Law 9 (red is the default and these five have been red since they were written); Law 1 (a reader re-deriving what `cairn review` does by reading the dispatcher is re-deriving a settled answer).
known_hole_inherited_knowingly: THE COMMAND LANE WALKS ONE WAY, and this ticket does not turn it around. It asks whether each executable in bin/cmd is named by some charter; it never asks whether each command a charter NAMES still exists. So a charter naming a command nobody can run is invisible. n=1 and it is inside this ticket's own scope: cairn/tools/operator_inbox's charter has named `cairn operator_inbox` while every caller in the corpus says `cairn operator`, and nothing ever reported it. The inverse check is NOT built here because extracting `cairn <word>` from prose invoke strings false-positives on bin's own literal `cairn <name> <args...>`, and a check that manufactures reds is worse than the gap. Recorded for a later cast.
